subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what should happen when a mutating tool fails but the assistant final reply sounds successful?
rationale: Source inspection proves the UX gap, but choosing `all | final | off` semantics changes public config and safety defaults for failed side effects, so automation cannot safely decide the product contract.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in delivery policy
options.body: Define a default-compatible enum that preserves current safety by default while allowing hosted or group-chat operators to choose final-only or off behavior with focused upgrade and channel tests.

options.title: Keep boolean-only policy
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off operator escape hatch and close or defer the success-aware enum request after documenting that boundary.

options.title: Move policy to channels
options.body: Let Telegram, Discord, Feishu, or other team-chat plugins own warning visibility where channel UX differs, avoiding another global message config key.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in delivery policy
recommendation.body: Define a default-compatible enum that preserves current safety by default while allowing hosted or group-chat operators to choose final-only or off behavior with focused upgrade and channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on the central warning-policy code and the merged related PR that explicitly left this broader issue open.
